trees.title: Is this interaction in scope of the Code?
trees.description: Determine if an interaction, event, or activity is governed by the MedTech Europe Code based on geography and affiliations.

nodes.text: What type of product or service is the interaction primarily linked to?
nodes.helpText: The Code governs interactions related to Medical Technologies, understood as those products under the scope of MDR and IVDR.

options.label: Medical Technologies (or a combination involving Medical Technologies)
Exclusively non-Medical Technologies (e.g., purely pharma or research-only products without MedTech link)

nodes.text: Who is initiating or conducting the interaction / activity on behalf of the company?

options.label: A Member Company Headquarter or a European Subsidiary
An affiliated subsidiary located OUTSIDE the MedTech Europe Area (e.g., US Affiliate)
A Third Party Intermediary (e.g., Distributor, Agent, PCO)

nodes.text: Does your company have a contractual relationship with the Third Party Intermediary (for example a distribution, agency or service agreement)?

options.label: Yes, we have a contract with them
No, they are a true reseller: they buy and resell our products with no contract with us

nodes.helpText: Chapter 10 covers any entity or person that markets, sells, promotes or otherwise brings the company’s products to end-users. Where the company has a contract with them, it must impose obligations to comply with the Code.

nodes.text: Where is the target Healthcare Professional (HCP) or Healthcare Organisation (HCO) registered and practicing?
nodes.helpText: Coverage is determined by the location of the HCP/HCO, regardless of where the actual activity takes place.

options.label: In a MedTech Europe Country (the EEA and the other countries in Annex III, e.g. the UK, Switzerland, Turkey, Israel)
In a Mecomed Territory: Africa (excluding South Africa)
In a Mecomed Territory: Middle East or Central Asia (Iran, Pakistan)
Rest of the World (e.g. North/South America, Asia Pacific, South Africa)
No specific HCP/HCO involved (e.g. organising a general event locally)

nodes.text: The HCPs themselves do not trigger the Code. However, where is the specific Activity or Event taking place?
nodes.helpText: The actual physical location of the event/interaction determines if the Code applies to the activity itself.

options.label: In a MedTech Europe Country (the EEA and the other countries in Annex III, e.g. the UK, Switzerland, Turkey, Israel)
In a Mecomed Territory (Africa excluding South Africa, Middle East, Iran, Pakistan)
Rest of the World (e.g. Americas, Asia Pacific, South Africa)

nodes.text: OUT OF SCOPE. The Code does not apply to interactions linked exclusively to non-Medical Technology products or services. It does apply as soon as an interaction is linked, even in part, to Medical Technologies, and another business unit or affiliate cannot be used to get around it.

NOT APPLICABLE. A true reseller with no contractual relationship with the company acts for its own business, and the Code does not directly govern its activities. As soon as the company enters into a contract with it, Chapter 10 applies: the contract must impose obligations to comply with the Code, with appropriate oversight.

IN SCOPE. Because the HCP/HCO is registered in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area, the Code applies as a minimum standard, regardless of where the activity takes place. An activity of an affiliated company located outside the Area is deemed attributable to the Member Company, and an intermediary acting under contract must be bound to comply with the Code (Chapter 10).
IN SCOPE. Even though the HCPs/HCOs are from outside the Area, the Activity takes place within the MedTech Europe Geographic Area, so the Code applies to it.

OUT OF SCOPE. Both the HCP/HCO and the intended Activity are located entirely outside of the MedTech Europe Geographic Area. The MedTech Europe Code does not apply, but local laws, regulations and codes (in South Africa, for example, the SAMED code) and your company’s own policies still do.

trees.title: Is My Event Location Compliant?
trees.description: Assess whether a proposed event location meets MedTech Europe Code requirements for venue selection.

nodes.text: Does the Code apply to this Event?
nodes.helpText: The Code applies to interactions with HCPs and HCOs registered and practising in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area wherever the Event takes place, and to Events held in the Area wherever the HCPs come from.

options.label: Yes: the Event takes place in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area, or HCPs registered and practising in the Area attend it
No: the Event takes place outside the Area and no HCPs from the Area attend it
I’m not sure

nodes.text: Will the Event be held in person?
nodes.helpText: An Event held in person and also broadcast online is not a Virtual Event: it must meet all the requirements for in-person Events.

options.label: Yes, in person (including a hybrid Event, broadcast online as well)
No, online only (a Virtual Event)

nodes.text: Is the Event location in or near a city or town that is a recognised scientific or business centre, suitable for an Event conducive to the exchange of ideas and the transmission of knowledge?
nodes.helpText: The location and venue should not become the main attraction of the Event.

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: Which of these best describes the venue?
nodes.helpText: The perceived image of the location and venue must not be luxury, tourist/holiday-oriented or that of an Entertainment venue.

options.label: A cruise ship, or a hotel with an on-site casino
A hotel or resort renowned for its leisure or entertainment facilities, or centred on recreation or sport (e.g. golf, private beach, ski or water sports)
A luxury venue, or one whose image is tourist/holiday-oriented or that of an Entertainment venue
None of these: a venue suited to professional meetings

nodes.text: Is the venue well adapted to business meetings, and is there a compelling need to use it, for example a lack of alternative venues or genuine safety or security issues?
nodes.helpText: Q&A 5 allows narrow exceptions to the rule against leisure venues, in an otherwise compliant geographic location.

options.label: Yes, and the need is documented
No

nodes.text: Is the location renowned as a seasonal vacation or holiday destination (e.g. a ski, island or beach resort), and does the Event fall, even in part, within that season?
nodes.helpText: The time of year must not be associated with a touristic season for the location. In Europe, the ski season is considered to run from December 20 - March 31 and the summer season from June 15 - September 15. Equivalent, seasonally adjusted dates apply in other regions of the world.

options.label: Yes, the Event falls within the season, at least in part
No

nodes.text: Is the location central, given where most invited participants live, and easy to reach (close to an airport and/or train station with appropriate international connections and reliable ground transport to the venue)?

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: The MedTech Europe Code does not apply to this Event, but local laws, regulations and codes and your company’s own policies should still be followed.

Whether the Code applies depends on where the Event takes place and where the attending HCPs are registered and practising. Use the “Is this interaction in scope of the Code?” tree first, then come back.

The location and venue criteria concern in-person Events. A Virtual Event must still comply with any part of the Code that by its nature applies to it, for example the programme requirements and Chapters 2, 3 and 4.

NOT ALLOWED. The Event location and venue should be in or near a city or town which is a recognised scientific or business centre, suitable for an Event conducive to the exchange of ideas and the transmission of knowledge.
NOT ALLOWED. For reasons of perception, cruise ships and hotels with on-site casinos are under no circumstances compliant with the Code, either as an Event venue or for HCPs’ accommodation.

NOT ALLOWED. The perceived image of the location and venue must not be luxury, tourist/holiday-oriented or that of an Entertainment venue. Member Companies may not pay for HCPs’ lodging at top category or luxury hotels either.

In principle NOT ALLOWED. It is not appropriate for a Member Company to organise or support Events at hotels or resorts renowned for their entertainment facilities or centred around recreational or sporting activities, unless there is a compelling need to use the venue.

A NARROW EXCEPTION MAY BE CONSIDERED. The Event’s promotional material must not feature the venue’s leisure aspects; the agenda must leave HCPs no time to use the leisure facilities during any significant part of a normal working day; and the company may not pay for their use. Accommodation separate from the venue may be required. The other location criteria, including the season, still apply.
NOT ALLOWED. Member Companies must not support or organise Events at seasonal vacation destinations during the season in question, even if only in part.

NOT ALLOWED IN PRINCIPLE. The Code requires the company to take into account that the location should be central for the majority of participants and easy to reach, close to an airport and/or train station with appropriate connections. Only an exceptional, well-documented justification, reviewed internally, could support going ahead.

No issue found on these points: the location and venue appear to meet Chapter 1, Section 2. Also check the rest of Chapter 1 to be sure: the programme, reasonable hospitality (no top category or luxury hotels), travel, no Guests, Employer Notification, and a CVS decision where one is needed.

trees.title: Is My Consulting Arrangement Compliant?
trees.description: Evaluate whether a proposed consulting arrangement with a Healthcare Professional or Healthcare Organisation meets Code requirements.

nodes.text: Was a Legitimate Business Need for the services identified in advance, before the consultant was selected?
nodes.helpText: Engaging a specific HCP or HCO for sales reasons is not a Legitimate Business Need.

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: Was the consultant selected through the company’s independent decision-making/review process, including a documented, prior evaluation of the risks and of the consultant’s background?
nodes.helpText: If the sales function has to be involved, the independent process must ensure the decision fulfils a Legitimate Business Need.

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: Was the consultant selected on criteria directly related to the identified need, such as their qualifications, expertise and experience?
nodes.helpText: The volume or value of business the consultant generates is not a relevant criterion.

options.label: Yes, selected on merit
No, selected for other reasons

nodes.text: Is the engagement free of any link to the consultant’s past, present or future purchase, recommendation, prescription or use of the company’s products or services?

options.label: Yes, there is no such link
No, or it could act as an inducement

nodes.text: Is there a written agreement, signed by the parties before the services start, that specifies the services, the basis for compensation and the expenses that can be claimed?

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: Is the compensation reasonable, within any limits set by local law, and set at Fair Market Value using the company’s documented method for determining it?

options.label: Yes
No, or it may be excessive

nodes.text: Before the services start, have all required consents and approvals been obtained (for example from the hospital administration or the HCP’s superior), or, where no national rules apply, has Employer Notification been made?

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: NOT ALLOWED. Consulting Arrangements must be entered into only where a Legitimate Business Need for the services is identified in advance, before the consultant is selected.

NOT ALLOWED. Member Companies shall select consultants through an independent decision-making/review process, with a documented, prior evaluation of the risks and of each prospective consultant’s background.
NOT ALLOWED. Consultants must be selected on criteria directly related to the identified need and their qualifications, expertise and experience, not on the volume or value of business they generate.

NOT ALLOWED. Consulting Arrangements shall not be contingent in any way on the consultant’s purchase, recommendation, prescription or use of the company’s products or services, and must not be an inducement to them.

NOT ALLOWED. The arrangement must be documented in a written agreement, signed by the parties before the services start, specifying the services, the basis for compensation and which expenses can be claimed.
NOT ALLOWED. Compensation must be reasonable, comply with local limits and reflect Fair Market Value, determined by a documented internal method. Excessive payments may be viewed as an inducement.

NOT ALLOWED YET. All required consents and approvals shall be obtained before the services start. Where no national requirements apply, the company shall require Employer Notification disclosing the purpose and scope of the arrangement.

No issue found on these points. Also check, to be sure: no more consultants than reasonably needed; potential conflicts of interest considered; records kept of the services and of how the company used them; the venue, hospitality and travel for meetings follow Chapter 1; the consultant must disclose their status as a consultant in related publications and presentations; and the arrangement is permitted under local law. These rules also apply to HCOs, and when a consultant declines a fee.

trees.title: Direct Support to HCP Participation in Events
trees.description: Determine if direct support for Healthcare Professional (HCP) attendance at an event is compliant based on Annex VI rules.

nodes.text: What type of event is the direct support intended for?
nodes.helpText: Support rules differ significantly depending on the event type. Signs of a Third Party Organised Event: it is open beyond the company’s customers, a third party sets the agenda and chooses the attendees (or HCPs self-select), it has CME accreditation or a broad focus. Single-sponsored events are often Company Events.

options.label: Third Party Organised Educational Conference (TPOE)
Third Party Organised Procedure Training meeting
Company Event

nodes.text: Does the training meet the criteria for a Third Party Organised Procedure Training?
nodes.helpText: Practical sessions must make up more than 50% of the programme and hands-on sessions at least one third, focused on medical procedures rather than products. A training organised in connection with, adjacent to or at the same time as a larger conference does not qualify (Annex VII, Q&A 18).

options.label: Yes: it stands alone, is mostly practical and is held mainly in a clinical environment
No, or it is held with, next to or at the same time as a larger conference
I don’t know

nodes.text: What is the specific setting within the Third Party Organised Educational Conference?
nodes.helpText: Support restrictions apply differently to the main event versus satellite symposia or booths.

options.label: Main Event / Independent Scientific Program
Satellite Symposium
Booth

nodes.text: What is the intended role of the Healthcare Professional at the Satellite Symposium or Booth?
nodes.helpText: Faculty are podium speakers, moderators or chairs who present during the Event and prepare in advance. Delegates attend passively; poster and abstract presenters count as Delegates.

options.label: Faculty / Speaker
Delegate

nodes.text: What type of Company Event is it?
nodes.helpText: Identify if the primary purpose is procedural training or general product/business promotion.

options.label: Product and Procedure Training and Education Event
Sales, Promotional and Other Business Meeting

nodes.text: Is the Product and Procedure Training and Education Event taking place at or about the same time as a Third Party Organised Educational Event?
nodes.helpText: Proximity to third-party events alters the compliance logic.

options.label: No (NOT at the same time)
Yes (At or about the same time)

nodes.text: What is the intended role of the Healthcare Professional across the events?
nodes.helpText: Faculty are podium speakers, moderators or chairs who present during the Event and prepare in advance. Delegates attend passively; poster and abstract presenters count as Delegates.

options.label: Faculty / Speaker
Delegate

nodes.text: Is the Sales, Promotional and Other Business Meeting taking place at or about the same time as a Third Party Organised Educational Event?
nodes.helpText: Proximity to third-party events alters the compliance logic.

options.label: No (NOT at the same time)
Yes (At or about the same time)

nodes.text: What is the intended role of the Healthcare Professional?
nodes.helpText: Faculty are podium speakers, moderators or chairs who present during the Event and prepare in advance. Delegates attend passively; poster and abstract presenters count as Delegates.

options.label: Faculty / Speaker
Delegate

nodes.text: What is the intended role of the Healthcare Professional across the events?
nodes.helpText: Faculty are podium speakers, moderators or chairs who present during the Event and prepare in advance. Delegates attend passively; poster and abstract presenters count as Delegates.

options.label: Faculty / Speaker
Delegate

nodes.text: NOT ALLOWED. Direct support for HCP attendance at the Main Event / Independent Scientific Program of a Third Party Organised Educational Conference is prohibited for both Faculty/Speakers and Delegates. The company can support the Conference through an Educational Grant instead.
nodes.reference: Annex VI — Third Party Organised Educational Conference

nodes.text: Direct support for HCP attendance at a Third Party Organised Procedure Training meeting is allowed for both Faculty/Speakers and Delegates. The training must still meet Chapter 1 (General Criteria for Events) and, where applicable, have CVS approval. If its hands-on part is cancelled or made virtual, it no longer qualifies, and travel may not be paid.

NOT ALLOWED. A training that does not meet the criteria is not a Third Party Organised Procedure Training. Treat it as a Third Party Organised Educational Conference: direct support for HCP attendance at its main programme is not allowed, for Faculty or Delegates. Support it through an Educational Grant instead.
Whether direct support is allowed depends on whether the training qualifies as a Procedure Training. Check its agenda with the TPPT Checker, then come back and answer.
Direct support for a Product and Procedure Training and Education Event that is NOT taking place at or about the same time as a TPOE is allowed for both Faculty/Speakers and Delegates.
Direct support for Delegates attending a Sales, Promotional and Other Business Meeting is generally NOT ALLOWED. Exception: Allowed ONLY for demonstration of non-portable equipment.
Direct support for HCP attendance is ALLOWED for Faculty/Speakers. Engage them under a written consulting agreement that meets Chapter 5 (Consulting Arrangements).
nodes.reference: Annex VI — Direct support for HCP attendance

nodes.text: Direct support for HCP attendance is ALLOWED for Faculty/Speakers. A consulting agreement is required (Chapter 5).
nodes.reference: Annex VI — Direct support for HCP attendance

nodes.text: Direct support for HCP attendance is NOT ALLOWED for Delegates in this scenario.
nodes.reference: Annex VI — Direct support for HCP attendance

trees.title: Conference Vetting System check
trees.description: Check in a few questions whether support for a Third Party Organised Educational Event needs a CVS decision under Annex I, and look up the Event’s current status in CVS.

required.intro: This support needs a positive CVS decision. Find the Event, and the right edition, in CVS to see its current status.

statuses.text: CVS has assessed the Event as Compliant. The decision is binding on all Member Companies, and the CVS requirement for this support is met. The Code and local laws and regulations still apply to the support itself.

The Event has been Pre-Cleared: only its geographic location and venue have received preliminary approval. A final Compliant assessment of the whole Event is still needed before this support can be provided.
The Event has not yet received a final CVS assessment (status “{status}”). Do not make a definitive commitment or provide this support unless and until the Event is assessed Compliant.

The Event was Not Pre-cleared: its geographic location or venue did not meet the applicable requirements. This support needs a positive CVS decision, so it cannot be provided while the Event has this status.
CVS has assessed the Event as Not Compliant. The decision is binding on all Member Companies, so this support, which needs a positive CVS decision, cannot be provided.
CVS did not assess the Event (status “{status}”), so there is no positive CVS decision and this support cannot be provided.

CVS has concluded that the Event is outside its scope, although your answers place this support within it. Clarify the Event’s audience with the organiser. Being outside CVS scope does not make the support permitted: the Code and local laws and regulations still apply.

required.otherStatus: “{status}” is not a CVS status this tree recognises. Check its meaning in CVS before relying on it.
required.noMatch: Based on your answers, the Event requires CVS assessment, but no matching Event was found. Submit the Event to CVS as soon as possible, or ask the organiser to do so. Do not provide this support unless and until the Event has been assessed Compliant.

national.intro: You expect a national Event. Check whether it has been submitted to CVS anyway: a CVS record suggests that the organiser or another Member Company expects Delegates from more than one country.

statuses.text: CVS has assessed the Event as outside its scope, which is consistent with a national Event.

national.otherStatus: You have indicated that this is a national Event, but the Event has been submitted to CVS (status “{status}”). The organiser or another Member Company may have different information about the countries from which HCP Delegates are expected to attend. Clarify the Event’s intended audience with the organiser and consider refraining from making a definitive commitment to provide support until the position is clear.

nodes.text: Where will the Event take place?
nodes.helpText: The MedTech Europe Geographic Area covers the countries of the European Economic Area and the other countries where Member Associations are located (Annex III), including the countries covered by Mecomed. For Events in countries covered by Mecomed, CVS applies Mecomed’s guidelines, whose scope covers national and regional Events as well as international ones. A hybrid Event, held in person with sessions also broadcast online, counts as held in person.

options.label: In the MedTech Europe Geographic Area, outside the countries covered by Mecomed
In a country covered by Mecomed (Africa excluding South Africa, the Middle East, Iran, Pakistan)
Outside the MedTech Europe Geographic Area
Online only (a Virtual Event)

nodes.text: Do you expect HCP Delegates from more than one country in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area to attend the Event?
nodes.helpText: Count the HCPs attending as Delegates, including poster and abstract presenters, but not the Faculty. Answer on the information available to your company, for example from the organiser, from your own support arrangements or from previous editions of the Event. You do not need to provide evidence. For a national Event, the result lets you check whether it has been submitted to CVS anyway.

options.label: Yes: HCPs from at least two countries of the Area (an international Event)
No: local HCPs only, from the country where the Event takes place (a national Event)
No: local HCPs, and HCPs from outside the Area
I don’t know

nodes.text: Will Member Companies support HCPs registered and practising in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area to attend the Event, for example through a grant that funds their attendance or a consultancy agreement as a speaker?
nodes.helpText: For an Event held outside the Area, what matters is whether Member Companies support the attendance of HCPs from the Area, not whether such HCPs attend at their own cost (Annex I, footnote 3). The Code applies to interactions with HCPs and Healthcare Organisations from the Area wherever the Event takes place.

options.label: Yes
No
I don’t know

nodes.text: Is the Event one of those that Mecomed exempts from CVS?
nodes.helpText: Mecomed’s CVS covers international, regional and national Third Party Educational Events. A local in-institution activity is exempt only if all its conditions are met.

options.label: A local in-institution activity: organised by an HCO on its own premises, with medical education for its own HCPs, no registration fees, no travel or accommodation costs, and any support given to the HCO, not to individual HCPs
A public awareness campaign for patients or the public, with no session addressed to HCPs
No, neither of these
I don’t know

nodes.text: What does the company plan to provide?
nodes.helpText: These are the types of support in Annex I. If the company plans several, check each one. Company representatives are the company’s own staff: an HCP engaged by the company is a speaker, not a representative.

options.label: Educational Grant to support the general running of the conference
Educational Grant that includes funds to support HCPs’ attendance
Educational Grant that includes funds to support Faculty
Consultancy agreement with a speaker in the company’s satellite symposium
Attendance of Member Company representatives (company staff)
Booth or advertising
Direct sponsorship of HCPs as Delegates (passive participation)
Direct sponsorship of HCPs as Faculty (active participation)

nodes.text: Will the grant fund the attendance of HCPs registered and practising in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area?
nodes.helpText: For an Event held outside the Area, a grant that funds HCPs’ attendance needs a CVS decision only when HCPs from the Area benefit from it (Annex I, footnote 3).

options.label: Yes
No
I don’t know

nodes.text: CVS approval not required but the Code and local laws and regulations still apply. The company checks the Event itself against the Code, including Chapter 1 (General Criteria for Events).

Formally a national Event: CVS approval is not required, but the Code and local laws and regulations still apply. Because HCPs from outside the Area also attend, it may be worth checking with CVS whether it considers the Event within its scope before relying on this. The company checks the Event itself against the Code, including Chapter 1 (General Criteria for Events).
Subject to CVS decision. The company may provide this support only once CVS has assessed the Event as Compliant.
Subject to CVS decision under Mecomed’s guidelines, whatever the Event’s audience. The company may provide this support only once CVS has assessed the Event as Compliant.

No CVS decision is needed: Mecomed exempts this kind of Event from CVS. The Code and local laws and regulations still apply to the support; the ban on direct sponsorship of HCPs and the internal review of company attendance still apply too.
Allowed. Not subject to CVS decision. The Code and local laws and regulations still apply.

No CVS decision is needed, because the grant does not fund the attendance of HCPs from the MedTech Europe Geographic Area (Annex I, footnote 3). The Code applies to the grant only if it goes to a Healthcare Organisation located in the Area (Annex I, footnote 5).

Out of scope of the application of the Code, unless the grant goes to a Healthcare Organisation located in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area: the Code then applies, but no CVS decision is needed (Annex I, footnote 5).

Annex I marks this N/A: when Member Companies support no HCPs from the MedTech Europe Geographic Area to attend an Event held outside the Area, the Code does not apply to this support, unless the grant goes to a Healthcare Organisation located in the Area. No CVS decision is needed then (Annex I, footnote 5).

Annex I marks this N/A: when Member Companies support no HCPs from the MedTech Europe Geographic Area, as speakers or Delegates, to attend an Event held outside the Area, the Code does not apply to this support.

Member Company prior internal review against Code principles required. Before going ahead, the company reviews internally whether this is appropriate under the Code’s principles, in particular image and perception, whatever the Event’s CVS status.

Not allowed. Annex I does not allow direct sponsorship of HCPs registered and practising in the MedTech Europe Geographic Area, whether as Delegates or as Faculty in the main programme, and a positive CVS decision does not change this. The company can support the Event through an Educational Grant instead. The company’s own satellite symposium or booth, and procedure trainings that meet the Annex VII criteria, have their own rules; the TPPT Checker checks a procedure training’s agenda.
No CVS decision is needed: Virtual Events are not subject to CVS. The Code and local laws and regulations still apply to the support.

Not allowed. The company may not directly sponsor HCPs to take part in a Third Party Organised Educational Event, as Delegates or as Faculty, and this applies to Virtual Events too. The company can support the Event through an Educational Grant instead.
Whether a CVS decision is needed depends on this answer. Find out, for example from the organiser, then go back and answer it.

trees.title: Grants and Charitable Donations
trees.description: Determine if you can provide a grant or donation to a specific entity, and evaluate what conditions can be lawfully imposed under the General Criteria.

nodes.text: General Criteria: Who is deciding upon, or approving, the provision of these funds?
nodes.helpText: Chapter 4 requires an independent decision-making/review process, with criteria that are not sales or commercially oriented, for example led by the legal, finance or compliance function.

options.label: The Sales or Commercial function is making/approving the decision
An independent function (e.g., Legal, Compliance, Finance)

nodes.text: General Criteria: Are these funds contingent in any way on past, present, or potential future purchases, leases, prescriptions, or recommendations of the Member Company’s products?

options.label: Yes, there is a commercial expectation or contingency
No, there is no commercial tie

nodes.text: General Criteria: How did the request for the funds reach the company?

options.label: A written request from the organisation, or a documented initiative of the company
From an HCP who is an employee or officer of the organisation, in writing on its behalf
From an HCP, in their own name

nodes.text: To what type of entity does the Member Company intend to provide the funds or in-kind support?

options.label: Individual Healthcare Professional (HCP)
A charity chosen or requested by an HCP (for example instead of a professional fee)
A Professional Conference Organiser or other for-profit company that is not an HCO
Patient Organisation
Hospital or other Healthcare Organisation (HCO)
Charitable or philanthropic organisation that is not an HCO

nodes.helpText: A Healthcare Organisation is any healthcare, medical or scientific organisation, whatever its legal form: for example a hospital, clinic, foundation, university or learned society (but not a patient organisation). A charity that meets this definition is an HCO.

nodes.text: What is the intended purpose of the funds provided to the Healthcare Organisation (HCO)?

options.label: Charitable Donation (philanthropic aid or financial support)
Educational Grant (e.g. supporting third-party events, or fellowships)
Research Grant
To cover the HCO’s normal overheads or routine operating costs

nodes.text: What will the funds pay for?
nodes.helpText: A for-profit organiser acting independently of any HCO cannot receive an Educational Grant, but funds earmarked for education are treated like one.

options.label: A commercial sponsorship: booth space, advertising or other consideration for the company
Funds earmarked for education, e.g. HCP Delegate places and expenses

nodes.text: Does one of these exceptions apply (and local law does not prohibit it)?
nodes.helpText: Routine costs are those that would fall under the HCO’s normal budget. An activity is not necessarily non-routine because it cannot run without funding.

options.label: A value-add in a lawful tender, related to that tender’s requirements
A Scholarship or Fellowship
A legitimate educational programme that improves patient safety or outcomes beyond normal hospital capacity
None of these

nodes.text: What is the intended purpose of the funds provided to the charitable/philanthropic organisation?

options.label: Charitable Donation (for philanthropic relief/charity)
Educational Grant (for advancement of medical education)
We are participating in their fundraiser (e.g., charity dinner, golf tournament)

nodes.helpText: Charitable Donations may be made only to charities or non-profit entities whose main purposes are charitable or philanthropic and which are objectively engaged in such activities.

nodes.text: Is the Charitable Donation to the hospital/HCO permitted in one of these ways?
nodes.helpText: Financial Hardship means extreme and unavoidable financial distress, outside the HCO’s control, where it cannot operate and patient care is jeopardised. Distress caused by mismanagement does not count. It must be documented and objectively substantiated.

options.label: Demonstrated Financial Hardship, and the donation benefits patients or is limited to specific needs identified in advance
The donation is explicitly permitted by applicable national law
Neither: it is a general donation to support the hospital

nodes.text: Are you inviting Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) to attend the fundraiser at the Member Company expense?

options.label: Yes, we intend to invite HCPs or suggest names to the organiser
No, tickets will be used internally by our employees or returned

nodes.text: What conditions or specifications does the Member Company intend to impose on the Charitable Donation?

options.label: We want to control the specific, final use of the funds by the recipient
We will specify a broad, general purpose (e.g., relief for a specific disaster) without final control
No specific controls; the recipient decides how to apply it within their philanthropic mandate

nodes.text: What conditions or controls does the Member Company intend to impose on the Educational Grant?
nodes.helpText: The Code demands extreme separation between providing funds and directing their use.

options.label: We intend to select, or proactively seek the names of, the individual HCP beneficiaries
We want to direct the educational programme content or select the Faculty (beyond recommending speakers or commenting when expressly asked)
We will provide objective criteria (e.g. specialty, country, years of practice) for the HCO to allocate the funds
No control: the HCO decides, under a written agreement that specifies the intended purpose and lets us verify its use

nodes.text: Are the objective criteria or the chosen hospital department so narrow that you can effectively identify the individual HCP beneficiaries upfront?
nodes.helpText: e.g., granting funds to a specific sub-department that only employs one or two specific doctors.

options.label: Yes, the final beneficiaries are practically known to us
No, the ultimate HCP beneficiaries are completely unknown to us

nodes.text: Does the grant support a Third Party Organised Educational Event (its general running, HCPs’ attendance or Faculty)?

options.label: Yes
No (e.g. a Scholarship, Fellowship or public awareness campaign)

nodes.text: NOT ALLOWED. The Member Company sales and/or commercial function shall not decide upon and/or approve decisions to provide Grants or Charitable Donations. An independent review process is mandatory.
NOT ALLOWED. Grants and Donations shall NEVER be contingent in any way on past, present or potential future purchase, lease, or recommendation of products.

NOT ALLOWED. Grants and Charitable Donations shall not be provided in response to requests made by HCPs, unless the HCP is an employee or officer of the qualifying organisation and submits the request in writing on its behalf.
NOT ALLOWED. A Member Company shall not provide Grants or Charitable Donations to individual Healthcare Professionals, or in the name of an HCP. Funds must go directly to the qualifying organisation.
NOT ALLOWED. It is not appropriate to support the favourite charity of a Healthcare Professional in response to a request by that HCP, whatever the reason, for example in lieu of a professional fee.

ALLOWED AS A COMMERCIAL SPONSORSHIP, not a Grant. Document it in a written commercial agreement and follow Chapter 2 (Third Party Organised Educational Events), including a CVS decision where Annex I requires one.

ALLOWED ONLY UNDER THE EDUCATIONAL GRANT RULES. All the Code provisions governing Educational Grants apply: the organiser alone selects the HCPs, the Event must have CVS approval where applicable, and the company publicly discloses the funding. Funds may not go to a travel agency directly.
NOT APPLICABLE. The Code does not cover Grants or Charitable Donations to Patient Organisations. Please refer to the MedTech Europe Patient Organisation Guidelines.
NOT ALLOWED. A Member Company cannot make a general Charitable Donation to support an HCO. Hospitals have health functions, not philanthropic functions as their main purposes.
NOT ALLOWED IN PRINCIPLE. As a matter of principle, Member Companies should not cover an HCO’s normal overheads or routine costs of operation, and none of the exceptions in Q&A 36 applies.

A Q&A 36 EXCEPTION MAY APPLY. A tender value-add must relate to that specific tender; Scholarships and Fellowships go only to HCOs where HCPs are in training, with no company involvement in selection; an educational programme must be transparent to the hospital administration, limited in time, above normal capacity, brand-agnostic and must not promote the HCO. The rules for Educational Grants still apply.
Research Grants are covered by Chapter 6 (Research), not by this tree.

NOT ALLOWED. An Educational Grant can only be provided to a Healthcare Organisation. If the charity also qualifies as an HCO (for example a foundation active in healthcare), go back and choose “Hospital or other Healthcare Organisation”.
NOT ALLOWED. Member Companies shall have no control over the specific, final use of funds they provide as Charitable Donations.
COMPLIANT. Specifying a broad, general purpose (e.g., relief of a specific disaster) is ALLOWED, provided the company carefully exercises NO control over the specific, final use.

COMPLIANT on these points. Charitable Donations to charitable or philanthropic organisations (or to hospitals in the permitted cases) are allowed without control over their final use. Also check: a written request with enough information for an objective evaluation, a written agreement signed before the donation, payment made to the organisation in its own name, and the company identified as the donor.
NOT ALLOWED. A Member Company shall not invite HCPs to attend a fundraiser at its expense, nor suggest names of HCPs to the sponsoring organisation.
COMPLIANT. Participating in fundraisers is ALLOWED provided tickets are used by employees or returned, and no HCPs are subsidized by the Member Company.

NOT ALLOWED. The receiving HCO shall be solely responsible for selecting the HCPs, and the grant agreement must say so. Member Companies should not proactively seek to receive the names of the HCP beneficiaries either (except where required by law, or after the Event for audit purposes).

NOT ALLOWED. The recipient HCO is solely responsible for the programme content and the selection of Faculty. Member Companies may recommend speakers or comment on the programme only if expressly asked.

NOT ALLOWED. Member Companies should not receive or be able to determine the names of the final HCP beneficiaries. Criteria or a hospital department so narrow that the beneficiaries are identifiable upfront defeat this (Q&As 30 and 31).

COMPLIANT on these points. The written agreement must specify the intended purpose, let the company verify the grant is used for it, and state that the HCO alone selects the beneficiaries. Also check: the grant is publicly disclosed under the Disclosure Guidelines; Scholarships and Fellowships go only to HCOs where HCPs are in training; public awareness campaigns do not promote the company’s products or specific HCOs; repeated grants to the same recipient are reviewed for perception risk.

ALLOWED ON THESE POINTS, SUBJECT TO THE EVENT. The Event must meet Chapter 1 (General Criteria for Events) and, where Annex I requires it, have a positive CVS decision: use the Conference Vetting System check. The written agreement must specify the intended purpose, let the company verify its use, and state that the HCO alone selects participants, programme and Faculty. Also check: public disclosure of the grant, and funds not paid to a travel agency directly.

trees.title: Educational and Promotional Items
trees.description: Determine if you can provide a specific item, gift, or prize to a Healthcare Professional or Healthcare Organisation.

nodes.text: What is the format or nature of the item the Member Company intends to provide?

options.label: Cash or cash equivalents
Evaluation Product, Demonstration Product, or Sample
Educational item, Promotional item, or Event Prize
Another gift (e.g. flowers, wine, a hamper or a personal present)

nodes.text: Are any of the following statements true regarding this specific item?
nodes.helpText: Select the statement that applies, or None.

options.label: It is intended to mark a significant life event (e.g., birthday, wedding)
It is being provided in response to a proactive request made by an HCP
It is an incentive to purchase products, or a gift in lieu of a declined consulting fee
None of the above.

nodes.text: Who is the direct, intended recipient of the Educational or Promotional Item?

options.label: Individual Healthcare Professional (HCP)
Healthcare Organisation (HCO) or hospital

nodes.text: What is the monetary value of the item being provided locally?

options.label: It is of Modest / Inexpensive value (within the limits of national laws, codes and Member Association guidelines)
It is an item of Greater value

nodes.text: Does the item relate to the HCPs’ practice, benefit patients or serve a genuine educational function, without being intended mainly for personal use?
nodes.helpText: For example, stationery or clinical wipes, as opposed to food, alcohol or items for the home or car.

options.label: Yes, it is relevant to their practice/educational and NOT mainly for personal use
No, it consists of food, alcohol, or is primarily for use in the home or car

nodes.text: What is the monetary value of the item being provided to the HCO?

options.label: It is of Modest / Inexpensive value
It is an educational item of Greater value (e.g., medical textbooks, anatomical models)

nodes.text: Does the higher value item serve a genuine educational function for the HCPs at the HCO, AND benefit patients, AND relate to the therapeutic areas in which the Member Company is interested or involved?

options.label: Yes, all three
No to at least one of them, or it is for HCPs’ personal use

nodes.text: Is this higher-value item offsetting the HCO normal overheads or routine costs of operation?

options.label: Yes, it covers routine operational overhead
No, it does not. (And we will maintain appropriate records of its provision)

nodes.text: NOT ALLOWED. Educational and promotional items must NEVER be given in the form of cash or cash equivalents.
NOT ALLOWED. It is generally prohibited to provide gifts to HCPs and HCOs. Only inexpensive educational or promotional items that meet Chapter 8 may be given.
OUT OF SCOPE. Please refer to Chapter 9 (Demonstration Products and Samples) or Chapter 6 (Research).

NOT ALLOWED. Items must not be given to mark significant life events, must not improperly reward or incentivise the use of the company’s products, and may not replace a declined consulting fee (Q&A 42).
STRONGLY RECOMMENDED AGAINST. No educational or promotional items should be provided in response to requests made by Healthcare Professionals.
NOT ALLOWED. Only items of modest/inexpensive value may be provided to an individual HCP. Greater value items can only be provided to an HCO.
NOT ALLOWED. Items cannot be mainly for personal/home/car use, nor consist of food/alcohol. They must relate to the HCP practice or benefit patients.
COMPLIANT on these points. Modest-value items related to practice, patients or education are allowed. A prize in a draw or competition at an Event must meet the same rules and national laws.

NOT ALLOWED. An educational item of greater value may be given to an HCO only if it serves a genuine educational function for its HCPs, benefits patients and relates to the company’s therapeutic areas, and not for HCPs’ personal use.

NOT ALLOWED IN PRINCIPLE. Higher value educational items should not be part of the HCO’s normal overheads or routine costs of operation. Only an exceptional, well-documented justification, reviewed internally, could support going ahead.
COMPLIANT on these points. A Member Company may occasionally provide an educational item of greater value to an HCO, and must keep appropriate records of it.

trees.title: Third Party Intermediaries (TPI)
trees.description: Evaluate the compliance and liability risks when engaging a Third Party Intermediary to act on your behalf.

nodes.text: Does the contractual documentation with the Third Party Intermediary (TPI) explicitly impose obligations to comply with the Code and other applicable guidelines?
nodes.helpText: Where local laws and regulations allow it, this is mandatory.

options.label: Yes, compliance obligations and appropriate oversight mechanisms are formally contracted
No, the contract does not include specific compliance obligations
Local laws and regulations do not allow such obligations

nodes.text: Has the Member Company performed a Risk Assessment and robust Due Diligence process on the TPI?
nodes.helpText: The Code recommends assessing the country and the intermediary’s risk profile, and a risk-based due diligence programme before engagement and at renewal.

options.label: Yes, we perform rigorous pre-engagement and renewal due diligence
No, due diligence or risk assessment has not been thoroughly performed

nodes.text: Does the company perform risk-based, routine monitoring, auditing or other assessment of the intermediary’s compliance, and ask it for regular confirmation of compliance?
nodes.helpText: The Code expects reasonable efforts, where applicable, to oversee intermediaries.

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: Does the company keep an up-to-date assessment of the intermediary’s training needs and train it regularly on the rules for its activity?

options.label: Yes
No

nodes.text: NOT ALLOWED. Member Companies SHALL ensure contractual documentation imposes obligations on the TPI to comply with the Code and provides for appropriate oversight.

The contractual obligation applies only where local laws and regulations allow it. Take legal advice, and apply the recommended risk assessment, due diligence, training and oversight as far as the law allows.

NOT ALLOWED IN PRINCIPLE. Member Companies should evaluate the risk profile of the intermediary and perform a robust, risk-based due diligence process before engaging it and at renewal. Only an exceptional, well-documented justification, reviewed internally, could support going ahead.

NOT ALLOWED IN PRINCIPLE. Member Companies should, where applicable, exercise reasonable efforts to perform risk-based, routine monitoring, auditing or other assessment of intermediaries, and should request regular confirmation of their compliance. Only an exceptional, well-documented justification, reviewed internally, could support going ahead.

STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. The Code recommends keeping an up-to-date assessment of the training needs of every intermediary and training them regularly on new rules, requirements and standards, where practical in local languages.

No issue found on these points. Also consider, to be sure: contract terms the Code encourages (compliance with laws, codes and company policies; independent audit rights, with access to books and records; early termination for non-compliance), regular confirmation of compliance from the intermediary, and corrective action if it fails to comply.
